label: caiso 54 daily gas
definition: (PROBE) caiso 54 daily-gas: caiso-53 recipe + --gas-hub-basis-daily, testing the caiso-53 root-cause item that the MONTHLY-average SoCal/PG&E citygate gas overlay is too blunt in spike months. Intakes daily CA Composite Average citygate spot (EIA NG Weekly compact table, 2023-2025, scripts/fetch_caiso_citygate_daily.py) and replaces the flat monthly hub level with a true-calendar-dated daily shape, mean-preserving on the measured monthly basis (annual gas burn/fuel mix unchanged) -- same construction as the NYISO daily Transco leg (dense trading-day quotes), not NEISO's sparse-narrative one. RESULT (official C3c, ordc.hoursGt200, same-environment A/B vs a fresh caiso-53 reproduction): 2023 454h(monthly)->455h(daily) vs 21h actual -- essentially UNCHANGED, NOT the collapse hypothesized. Day-level attribution explains why: the daily series correctly REDISTRIBUTES the tail rather than shrinking it. The measured citygate genuinely collapsed only in the LAST WEEK of Jan-2023 ($7.80-11.50/MMBtu) -- those days correctly drop from 9-19 tail-hours/day to ZERO. But days 2-18 (measured $16-24/MMBtu) are ABOVE the monthly average once the cheap last week is excluded, so they gain tail-hours instead (max zonal LMP $219.9->up to $282.9). Net Jan effect ~505->489h (own recompute), a real but marginal ~3% reduction. CONCLUSION: the monthly-average blunting is a real, now-fixed defect (last week was wrongly priced high before), but it is NOT the primary driver of the ~450h-vs-21h over-prediction -- most of January 2023 was persistently elevated in the real citygate market, not spike-concentrated in a way a monthly average would blunt. NEW ROOT-CAUSE ITEM (logged, not chased): the dominant driver of the residual ~450h/21h gap is something else -- CT_PEAKER's ct_netload_drag floor (forced share 40-62% per this bundle's D-2) and/or ra_mustoffer_bridge are candidates, or a genuine actual-side effect (demand response / oil-switching / imports) the model lacks; investigate separately per rule #1, no floor forcing. The daily-basis input is kept in code on its own physical merits (correct day-to-day delivered fuel cost, rule #13) independent of whether it moves C3c -- a real market behaviour is not reverted because the residual didn't move (rule #1). Not promoted; caiso-51/caiso-53 remain keeper. legitimacy_diagnostics attached (D-5 caiso_ra_mustoffer gap is pre-existing/documented on caiso-53 already, not introduced here).
